title: Finite limits after restricting a flat sheaf to a slice
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site, let $U$ be an object, and let $\mathcal F$ be flat. Then the tensor functor $\mathcal G \mapsto \mathcal G \otimes_{\mathcal O_U} \mathcal F|_U$ preserves finite limits on the slice site.

proof.text: Given a finite-limit diagram of modules on the slice, apply the sheafified direct-sum extension by zero. The extension exactness equivalence identifies its finite-limit cone with the extension of the original cone.

Tensor the extended diagram with the flat sheaf on the original site, so its finite limits are preserved. The natural extension-by-zero tensor comparison identifies this tensor diagram with the extension of the restricted tensor diagram.

Use the reverse implication of the extension exactness equivalence, or equivalently its cone reflection, to reflect the finite-limit comparison back to the slice. This is precisely preservation of finite limits by tensoring with the restriction.
